workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§105–108
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§105–108: The Muster Against the Merkid
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§105–108, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Four sections, one campaign taking shape. In §105 Temüjin sends Qasar and Belgütei to Jamuqa; To'oril's word follows, and Jamuqa answers with his grief for Börte and a plan against the three Merkid chiefs, naming where each lies. In §106 Jamuqa sends his own answer, a list of the gear he has readied and a place to meet. §107 has the armies set out, and §108 brings them to Botoqan-Boqorji, where Jamuqa, three days early, reproaches them for being late.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.l: Temüžin, Qasar, Belgütei, the three, from Toγ̇oril Qān returning, to-their-own-tent arriving,
sentences.i: Temüjin, Qasar and Belgütei, the three of them, came back from Qan To'oril and reached their own tent.
sentences.n: A plain converb chain: qarižu 'turning back' and kürčü 'arriving' hang on what follows. Ming 囘著 and 到着 mark them with 着, its sign for the converb. Qān-(n)ača is the ablative -(n)ača, 'from', glossed 自; the title qān stands after the name, Toγ̇oril Qān. In ger-tür(i)-jen the dative-locative -tür(i) (Ming 行) is followed by the reflexive-possessive -jen, 'to their own tent'; the (i) is Shiratori's. The unit stops here because the clause is not finished: the main verb is ilerün in the next one.

sentences.l: Temüžin, to Žamuqa, Qasar, Belgütei, the two (acc.), sending: "Žamuqa to-sworn-brother say" saying, speaking, sending,
sentences.i: Temüjin sent Qasar and Belgütei, the two, to Jamuqa, telling them to say to his sworn brother Jamuqa:
sentences.n: Temüžin is the subject; qojar-i (Ming 兩箇 行) is the pair Qasar and Belgütei as object, and Žamuqa-dur (行) is the place they are sent to. ilerün is ile- 'send' with the converb of time -rün (Ming 使去 'send'); the second ilerün is glossed only 去 'go', so 'going' is possible there. ügüle is the bare stem used as an imperative, 'say!', and keġen closes the quotation. anda is the 'sworn brother', the pledged friend of the chronicle, here Jamuqa. The message follows in the next units.

sentences.t: γurban Merkid-te irežü oro-ban hoγtorγu bolγaγdaγ̇a bi.

morph.gloss: the Merkid, a people [種名 行]
dative-locative (front-vowel form); here marks the agent, 'by the Merkid' (uncertain)

sentences.l: Three, by-the-Merkid, having-come, own-place empty was-made, I.
sentences.i: "The three Merkid came, and my own place was left empty.
sentences.n: The Ming marks Merkid-te with 行, the dative-locative marker, and the verb is a passive, so I read the dative as the agent, 'by the Merkid'; that is a reading, not a certainty. oro-ban (Ming 位, 'position') is the place one holds; it is the same spelling as oro 'hollow of the chest' used in a later unit. The message begins here; its closing quotation mark stands on bida in word 45. bolγaγdaγ̇a is bol- 'become' with a causative -γa- and a passive -γda-, 'was made'; the last ending is uncertain.

sentences.t: Onor nigenten busutu bida ösül(i)-jen ker ösekün

morph.gloss: nock, the notch of an arrow (so read from onolaba; the Ming 扣子 is 'button, fastening') [(扣子)]
collective plural, 'those of ...' (compare -tan in Žaqaγambu-tan; uncertain)

sentences.l: Nock one-ers, not-so are we? Own-enmity how to-repay?
sentences.i: Are we not of one nock? How shall we repay our enmity?
sentences.n: Hard to read; I give it as two questions. Onor is the arrow-nock (the Ming 扣子 means a button or fastening; I take it as the notch, from onolaba 'to nock' later in the text), and nigenten is nigen 'one' with the collective -ten, 'the ones of one nock', that is, men of one stock. busutu (Ming 不是有的麽, 'is it not so?') is the form of a rhetorical question; I cannot analyse it with confidence. ösül(i)-jen is 'one's own enmity' (Ming 讐 自的; the published parts have ösül 'enmity'); ösekün is the verb öse- 'repay' as printed (Ming 報), in an ending -kün I do not know, compare hačilaqun in a later unit.

sentences.t: ebür(i)-jen hemtüldeġe bi;

sentences.l: Own-bosom half-taken was, I;
sentences.i: my own bosom is half torn away;
sentences.n: ebür(i)-jen, 'one's own bosom' (Ming 懷 自的), is the figure of lap or breast for kin. hemtüldeġe is hemte 'half' made a verb, hemtül-, with a passive -de- and a past ending -ġe, read by analogy with bolγaγdaγ̇a in the unit above (-γda- ... -γ̇a); the Ming 被去了一半 says 'half taken away'. I am not sure of either ending.

is it not so? (rhetorical-question form; analysis uncertain, perhaps busu 'not, other' + -tu) [不是有的麽]

sentences.i: are we not the liver's offspring, kin?
sentences.n: heligen-ü is helige 'liver' with the n that the stem takes before a case ending, then the genitive -ü (Ming 肝的); uruγ is usually 'descendants', but the Ming writes 親 'kin'. Another rhetorical busutu. Liver is the seat of close kinship in Mongol speech.

sentences.i: How are we to repay our enmity?" So he said, and this was all the word he sent.
sentences.n: hačilaqun is hači 'enmity' made a verb with -la- and given an ending -qun (Ming 報的) which I take as a participle, 'to repay'; its sense is guesswork. ilegsen is the past participle of ile- 'send', 'what was sent', and edüi (Ming 這些) is 'only so much', a closing phrase.

sentences.l: Again, the Kereid's Toγ̇oril Qān's spoken words (acc.), to Žamuqa speaking, sending.
sentences.i: He also sent word to Jamuqa, giving the words that Qan To'oril of the Kereid had spoken.
sentences.n: Kereid-ün is the genitive of the people name (Ming 種名 的), and Qān-(n)u is the genitive of the title with the (n) Shiratori prints. ügülegsen üges-i is 'the words (üge + plural -s) spoken (-gsen) as object'. The ending of üges-i is the accusative (Ming 每(行)).

sentences.t: Erte üdür Jesügei Qān ečige-de min-u tusa said kigdegsen-i sedkižü nököčesü bi.

morph.gloss: Yesügei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
ruler, khan (title, set after the name) [皇帝]
my, of me (bi, genitive stem min- + -u, set after its noun) [我的]

sentences.l: Formerly, day: Jesügei Qān to-father, my help good done (acc.), thinking, companion-let-me-be, I.
sentences.i: "In the old days, remembering the good service done to my father Yesügei Qan, I will be your companion.
sentences.n: To'oril's words, sent to Jamuqa by way of Temüjin's messengers. ečige-de is 'father' in the dative (Ming 父 行), so the old Qan is called 'father' (as the elder sworn friend, I take it); min-u is 'my' placed after its noun; tusa said is 'help, good'; kigdegsen-i is ki- 'do' with a passive and the past participle plus the accusative, 'what was done' (Ming 被做了的 行). The passive leaves the doer open, and the English keeps it open: whether To'oril served Yesügei or the reverse the form does not say. nököčesü is nököče- 'be a companion' with the optative -sü, 'let me be a companion'. There is no opening quotation mark in the print; the closing one stands at the end of word 95.

sentences.t: Qojar tümed bolžu baraγ̇un γar bolun morilasu.
sentences.l: Two tümens making, right hand being, let me mount.
sentences.i: I will mount with two tümens, and be your right hand.
sentences.n: Two tümens are two units of ten thousand men (tümed is tümen with the plural -d, Ming 萬每). bolun is bol- 'become' with the converb -un, 'being'; with γar 'hand' and baraγ̇un 'right' it is 'being the right hand'. morilasu is mori 'horse' made a verb with -la- and given the optative -su, 'let me mount'.

sentences.t: Žamuqa deġü-de keleležü ile.

morph.gloss: Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to send (bare stem, here an imperative: 'send!'; uncertain) [去]

sentences.l: Žamuqa younger-brother-to speaking, send!
sentences.i: Send word to my younger brother Jamuqa.
sentences.n: deġü-de is deġü 'younger brother' in the dative (Ming 弟 行), the title the older man gives Jamuqa. keleležü is kele- 'speak' with -le- and the converb -žü. ile is the bare stem of ile- 'send' used as an imperative; Ming 去.

sentences.t: Žamuqa deġü qojar tümed morilatuγai.

morph.gloss: Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Žamuqa, younger-brother, two tümens let-mount.
sentences.i: Let my younger brother Jamuqa mount with two tümens.
sentences.n: morilatuγai is the same verb as morilasu, now with the third-person optative -tuγai (Ming 上馬敎, 'cause to mount'), so 'let him mount'. qojar tümed (Ming 二 萬每) is 'two tümens'. The speech is To'oril's, still addressed to the messengers.

sentences.t: Qamtudqu bolžaγ̇an Žamuqa deġü-dēče boltuγai" keġebe.

morph.gloss: to be together, to join (from qamtu 'together'; stem inferred; Ming 相合) [相合的]
to appoint, to agree on a meeting (stem inferred) [約會]
Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: The joint appointment, Žamuqa younger-brother-from, let it be" said.
sentences.i: Let the joint meeting be appointed by my younger brother Jamuqa," he said.
sentences.n: Qamtudqu is a participle of a verb I give as qamtud- 'be together' (Ming 相合的); bolžaγ̇an is 'appointment, meeting' (Ming 約會), and I do not know the exact ending. deġü-dēče has the ablative -dēče, 'from', so the arrangement of the meeting is to come 'from' Jamuqa. boltuγai is bol- with the optative, 'let it be'. The closing quotation mark stands on boltuγai in the print.

sentences.t: Ede üges-i daġusugan baražu Žamuqa ügülerün:

sentences.i: When these words had all been delivered, Jamuqa said:
sentences.n: daġusugan (Ming 敎盡, 'cause to be finished') and baražu (了着, 'being finished') together mean the telling was done. I give daġusugan the stem daġusu- 'to end' with the causative -γa- (the Ming 敎) and the converb -n, 'having made an end'; the stem is inferred. ügülerün is ügüle- with -rün; it opens the speech that follows.

sentences.t: "Temüžin anda-ji oro hoγtorγu bolba.

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
sworn brother, pledged friend [契合 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel-final stem)

sentences.l: Temüžin, sworn-brother (acc.), the hollow-of-chest empty became.
sentences.i: "My sworn brother Temüjin's breast has been left empty.
sentences.n: oro is 'hollow of the chest' (Ming 心窩, 'heart-pit'); hoγtorγu is 'empty'. anda-ji is anda with the accusative -ji; the grammar puts him as object, while the English wants a possessor. The quotation mark that opens Jamuqa's speech is printed before Temüžin.

sentences.l: Saying, knowing, heart my hurt.
sentences.i: Knowing it, my heart hurts.
sentences.n: keġen medežü, literally 'saying, knowing', is the Mongol way of putting a thought in a quotation and then going on from it; Ming 麽道 and 知着. min-u is 'my' placed after its noun, öre 'heart'. ebedbe is ebed- 'hurt' (Ming 痛了) in the past.

sentences.t: Ebür hemterebe keġen medežü helige min-u ebedbe.

morph.gloss: to be halved (from hemte 'half'; stem inferred) [半了]

to hurt, to be sick [痛了]

sentences.l: Bosom half-became, saying, knowing, liver my hurt.
sentences.i: Knowing that his bosom is half gone, my liver hurts.
sentences.n: Bosom and liver are paired as the seat of kin. hemterebe (Ming 半了) is the same verb as hemtüldeġe above, in the past; helige is 'liver'. The same keġen medežü as in the line before.

sentences.t: Ösül(i)-jen ösen Uduid, Uwas Merkid-i ülüdkežü Üžin-Börte-jen aburaja

morph.gloss: enmity, grievance to be repaid (as the published ösül ösün; Ming 讐 'enmity') [讐 自的(行)]
the Uduid, a Merkid clan (Ming 姓氏 'clan name') [姓氏]

Üjin-Börte, a woman's name (one two-part name) [婦人名]

sentences.l: Own-enmity repaying, Uduid, Uwas Merkid (acc.) destroying, Üžin-Börte own rescue-let-us.
sentences.i: Let us repay our enmity, destroy the Uduid and Uwas Merkid, and rescue Üjin Börte.
sentences.n: ösen has the Ming gloss 報 'repay'; I give it öse- (the stem as printed; Ming 報 'repay') with an ending -n, uncertain; it runs parallel to hači-jan aburan in the next unit. Uduid and Uwas are clan names (Ming 姓氏) of the Merkid; Merkid-i takes the accusative. ülüdkežü is a converb 'destroying' (Ming 殘滅着). aburaja is abura- with the hortative -ja, 'let us ...'; the Ming 救 says 'rescue, save'. Üžin-Börte-jen has the reflexive-possessive, so 'one's own Üžin-Börte', here 'our own'.

sentences.t: Hači-jan aburan qamuγ Qaγ̇ad-Merkid-i qaltačižu qatun Börte-jüġen qariγ̇ulun aburaja.

morph.gloss: enmity, vengeance, a feud [讐 (自的行)]
to requite, repay (Ming 報; perhaps the same verb as aburaja 'save', uncertain) [報]

morph.gloss: the Qa'at, a Merkid clan (Ming 姓氏 'clan name') [姓氏 種名 行]
to break, to smash (stem inferred from the Ming 破) [破着]
lady, queen, wife of a khan (noun) [娘子]

sentences.l: Own-enmity repaying, all the Qaγ̇ad Merkid (acc.) smashing, lady Börte own, bringing back, rescue-let-us.
sentences.i: Let us repay our enmity, break all the Qa'at Merkid, bring the lady Börte back and rescue her.
sentences.n: aburan has the Ming gloss 報 'repay', and aburaja 救 'rescue'; they look like one stem, abura-, and I cannot say how the two senses join (perhaps 'set right'). qaltačižu (Ming 破着) is 'smashing'. qariγ̇ulun is qari- 'turn back' with the causative -γ̇ul- and the converb -un, 'making her return'; the Ming gloss is only 囘着. Börte-jüġen is the reflexive-possessive in its longer form, 'her own'. aburaja appears twice with the Ming gloss 救咱.

sentences.t: Edöġe tere gölme dabšiqui-dur köġürge-jin daγ̇u bolγažu kökideg Toγtoγ̇a Nuγ̇ura keġer-e bi že.

morph.gloss: that, that one; also he, she (demonstrative and third-person pronoun) [那]
saddle-cloth (Ming 鞍韂 'saddle and saddle-cloth') (noun) [鞍韂]

words.reading: 荅卜失(中灰)-突︀舌兒 dabšiqui-dur

morph.gloss: to slap, to beat (stem inferred from the Ming 拍) [拍 時]
genitive: of (after a vowel-final stem; the j is Shiratori's glide)
to startle (stem inferred; Ming 輕驚動 'easily startled') [輕驚動的]

Nu'ura, a place name (Ming 地名) [地名]

sentences.l: Now, that saddle-cloth when-slapping, drum's sound making, easily-startled Toγtoγ̇a, Nuγ̇ura steppe-on, is, so.
sentences.i: Now Toqto'a, easily startled, who makes a drum's sound of a slapped saddle-cloth, is out on the steppe of Nu'ura.
sentences.n: The Ming reads tere gölme dabšiqui-dur köġürge-jin daγ̇u bolγažu as 'when that saddle-cloth is slapped, making a drum's sound', and kökideg as 輕驚動的 'easily startled'; so the epithet. I read bolγažu 'making' as Toγtoγ̇a's doing, a man who makes a drum's sound out of a slapped saddle-cloth; that is a reading, the Ming gives no more than the words. keġer-e is keġer 'open ground' with the dative-locative (Ming 野甸行). bi is 'is' here (Ming 有), not 'I', and že is a particle of assent, 'so'. Nuγ̇ura is a place name, 地名.

sentences.l: Lidded quiver when-shaken, rebelling Dair-Usun, now Orqon, Seleṅge of-the-two between Talγun islet-on is, so.
sentences.i: Dair-Usun, who rebels at the rattle of a lidded quiver, is now on the island of Talqun, between the Orqon and the Selenge.
sentences.n: Same pattern as the line before: a figure of quick fear, qor darbalžaqui-dur 'when the quiver is shaken' (Ming 搖閃 時, 箭筒), and an epithet, daižiγči (Ming 反的, 'one who turns against'; the stem is my inference). dabčitu is dabči 'lid' (Ming 葢子) with -tu. qojar-un žaγ̇ura is 'of the two, between'. Aral-a is 'island, islet' (Ming (洲)) with the dative-locative. Talγun is a place name.

sentences.t: Qamqa ulsun keisküi-dür qara hoi temečegči Qaγ̇atai-Darmala edöġe Qaraži keġer-e bi že;

morph.gloss: a steppe plant, Ming 蓬 'fleabane, tumbleweed' (noun) [蓬]
to blow, of the wind (stem uncertain; Ming 風刮) [風刮 時]
to contend, to strive (stem inferred; Ming 爭) [爭的]

words.reading: 中合阿台-荅舌兒馬剌 Qaγ̇atai-Darmala

morph.gloss: Qa'atai-Darmala, a man's name (personal name, one two-part name) [人名]
Qaraji, a place name (Ming 地名) [地名]
is, are (verb, short form; Ming 有) [有]
particle, 'indeed, so' (the Ming 也者 'so be it') [也者︀]

sentences.l: Qamqa, ulsun when-the-wind-blows, black wood contender, Qaγ̇atai-Darmala, now Qaraži steppe-on is, so;
sentences.i: Qa'atai-Darmala, who contends with the black wood when the wind blows on the qamqa and ulsun, is now on the steppe of Qaraji;
sentences.n: Qamqa (Ming 蓬 'fleabane, tumbleweed') and ulsun (蒿 'wormwood') are two dry steppe plants; keisküi-dür (風刮 時) is 'at the blowing of the wind'. temečegči (Ming 爭的) is 'one who strives, contends'. The line is the figure of a man who starts at a rustle, like Toqto'a and Dair-Usun, but how 'qara hoi temečegči' belongs to the plants I am not sure: the Ming gives no joint. Qaraži is a place name, 地名.

sentences.t: edöġe bida dötelen Kilqo müren-(n)i kiṅgüs Saqal-Bajan esen atuγai.

morph.gloss: straight on, directly (adverb; Ming 超直 'leaping straight'; analysis uncertain) [超直]
the Kilqo, a river (Ming 河名) [河名]
across, crosswise (Ming 橫斷 'cutting across'; analysis uncertain) [橫斷]
Saqal-Bajan (Ming 猪鬃草 'boar-bristle grass'; saqal 'beard', bajan 'rich'; a place or a plant, uncertain) [猪︀鬃草]
optative: let it be, let it stay

sentences.l: Now we, straight across, the Kilqo river (acc.) cutting-across, Saqal-Bajan safe let-be.
sentences.i: Now let us go straight across the Kilqo river, and let Saqal-Bajan stay safe.
sentences.n: Hard to read. dötelen (Ming 超直, 'leaping straight') and kiṅgüs (橫斷, 'cutting across') both say 'across', and I take them as two adverbs. Saqal-Bajan is glossed 猪鬃草 'boar-bristle grass'; saqal is 'beard', bajan 'rich'; it may be a name of a place or a person, or just the plant. esen is 'safe, whole' and atuγai is a- 'be' with the optative -tuγai, 'let it stay'.

sentences.t: Sal hujažu oroja.
sentences.l: Raft tying, let-us-enter.
sentences.i: Let us tie a raft and go in.
sentences.n: sal is a raft (Ming 筏子), hujažu is huja- 'tie, knot' with the converb -žu, and oroja is oro- 'enter' with the hortative -ja. The Ming for oroja is 入咱 'let us enter'; the English 'go in' leaves it open whether the river or the raft is entered; I take the river.

essential, vital, principal (Ming 緊要的 'important') [緊要的]

sentences.l: That easily-startled Toγtoγ̇a's smoke-hole above, his, entering, the essential door-frame his collapsing, colliding,
sentences.i: Let us come in at the top of the smoke-hole of that startled Toqto'a, and strike so that the frame of his tent falls in,
sentences.n: erüge is the roof-window or smoke-hole of a tent (Ming 天窻 'skylight'), and deġere is 'on top, above'; in-ü is 'his' set after its noun. eġede is 'door, door-frame'; here the Ming says 帳房骨子 'tent frame'. embürü and daγ̇arižu are converbs (Ming 塌了 'fallen in', 撞着 'colliding'); the stem embür- is inferred from the Ming. The subject is 'we' from the hortatives that surround the clause.

sentences.t: eme köġün in-ü ečültele qaγ̇uluja;

to be finished, used up (stem inferred; Ming 盡絕) [盡絕了]
to raid, to plunder, to ruin [毀了咱]

sentences.l: Wife, son, his, until-ended, let-us-ruin;
sentences.i: let us ruin him until his wives and sons are finished;
sentences.n: ečültele is ečül- 'be finished' (stem inferred, Ming 盡絕了) with the converb -tele, 'until'. qaγ̇uluja is qaγ̇ul- 'plunder, ruin' with the hortative -ja; the Ming gives 毀了咱 here and 毀滅咱 at the end of the section.

sentences.t: qutuγ eġede in-ü quγ̇uru daγ̇arižu

morph.gloss: fortune, blessing (Ming 福神的 'of the fortune-spirit') [福︀神︀的]
door, doorway, door-frame (noun; Ming here 帳房骨子 or 門框, 'tent-frame', 'door-frame') [門框]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to break, snap (stem inferred; Ming 折了) [折了]
to strike against, to pass by (Ming 撞着 'colliding'; elsewhere 經過) [撞着]

sentences.l: Fortune door-frame his breaking, colliding,
sentences.i: let us strike so that the door-frame of his fortune breaks,
sentences.n: qutuγ is 'blessing, fortune' (Ming 福神的, 'of the fortune-spirit'), I read qutuγ eġede as 'the fortune door-frame'; the Ming gives only 福神的 and 門框, and any picture of a spirit living in it is my guess. quγ̇uru (Ming 折了) is quγ̇ur- 'to break' with the converb -u; the stem is inferred.

sentences.t: qotola ulus-i in-ü qoγ̇osun boltala qaγ̇uluja.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to raid, to plunder, to ruin [毀滅咱]

sentences.l: All, people (acc.) his, until-empty-becoming, let-us-ruin.
sentences.i: and let us ruin all his people until nothing is left of them."
sentences.n: qotola (Ming 都行) is 'all, altogether'. boltala is bol- with the converb -tala, 'until it becomes', Ming 到了; qoγ̇osun is 'empty'. The section ends here; Jamuqa speaks again at the head of §106 (basa, 'again').

sentences.t: Žamuqa basa ügülerün: "Temüžin anda, Toγ̇oril Qān aqa qojar-a ügüle" keġen ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
converb of time: saying, when saying
Temüjin, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
To'oril, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
ruler, khan (title, set after the name) [皇帝]
to speak, to say (bare stem, here an imperative: 'say!') [說]
converb that closes a quotation: saying
converb of time: saying, when saying

sentences.l: Žamuqa again speaking: "Temüžin sworn-brother, Toγ̇oril Qān elder-brother, to-the-two say" saying, speaking:
sentences.i: Jamuqa spoke again: "Say to the two of them, to my sworn brother Temüjin and to my elder brother Qan To'oril," and he continued:
sentences.n: The speaker is Jamuqa, talking to the messengers, who are to carry his answer; qojar-a (Ming 兩箇行) is 'to the two'. ügüle is again the bare stem as an imperative, 'say!'. aqa is 'elder brother', the title Jamuqa gives To'oril. The speech after this is a message to be delivered, so the Mongol speaks in the first person while the carriers recite it.

sentences.t: "Bi bürün qaraγ̇atu tuk(i)-jan sačuba bi.

morph.gloss: converb of time: being; after bi, 'as for me' (Ming 呵)
a far view (stem inferred from qara- 'to look'; Ming 遠看見的 'seen from afar') [遠看(見)的]
standard, banner (so read; the Ming 英頭 is 'hero-head' and the stem is uncertain) [英頭 自的行]
to sprinkle a libation, to sacrifice (stem inferred; Ming 祭了也) [祭了也]

sentences.l: I, as-for, far-seen banner my-own sprinkled, I.
sentences.i: "As for me, I have made offering to my banner that is seen from afar.
sentences.n: Bi bürün, 'I being' (Ming 我 呵, 'as for me'), is a topic phrase. qaraγ̇atu is a stem I infer from qara- 'look', meaning 'seen from far', with -tu 'having'; the Ming 遠看見的 is 'seen from far', though it could also be read 'far-seeing'. tuk(i)-jan has the Ming 英頭, 'hero-head', and I take the word as the standard or banner; the stem is uncertain. sačuba is saču- 'sprinkle' in the past; the Ming 祭 shows an offering was made to it, presumably a libation.

sentences.t: Qara buγa-jin arasun(i)-jar bürigsen bürkiren büküi daγ̇utu köġürge-ban deledbe bi.

morph.gloss: bull (Ming 强牛 'strong ox') [强牛 的]

words.reading: 阿舌剌孫你-牙舌兒 arasun(i)-jar

morph.gloss: skin, hide (noun; Ming 皮子) [皮子敎]
instrumental: with, by means of (back-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's)
to cover, to stretch over (stem inferred; Ming 幔了的) [幔了的]
booming, drumming (sound word; Ming 鼕鼕 'boom-boom'; perhaps bürkire- + -n) [鼕鼕]
to beat, to strike (stem inferred; Ming 打了也) [打了也]

sentences.l: Black bull's hide-with covered, booming being, voiced drum my-own beaten, I.
sentences.i: I have beaten my drum, covered in black bull's hide, with its booming voice.
sentences.n: Qara buγa-jin is 'of the black bull' (Ming 强牛 的), arasun(i)-jar the instrumental of 'hide' (Ming 皮子敎, where 敎 marks 'with'). bürigsen (幔了的) is 'covered'; bürkiren (鼕鼕) is a sound word, 'boom-boom'; büküi is 'being'. daγ̇utu is daγ̇u 'voice' with -tu, 'voice-having', that is, sounding. köġürge-ban is the drum with the reflexive-possessive -ban; deledbe is deled- 'beat' in the past (stem inferred).

sentences.t: Qara qurdun(i)-jan unuba bi.

morph.gloss: fast; a fast horse (Ming 快馬) [快馬 自的行]

sentences.l: Black own-fast-horse rode, I.
sentences.i: I have mounted my black fast horse.
sentences.n: qurdun means 'fast' and also 'a fast horse' (Ming 快馬). The reflexive -(i)jan (自的行) again: 'my own'. unuba is unu- 'ride' in the past. A run of short parallel lines follows: each names a piece of gear and a verb of readiness.

sentences.t: Qataṅγu deġel(i)-jen emüsbe bi.

morph.gloss: steel-hard, hardened (adjective; Ming 鋼硬 'hard as steel') [鋼硬]
to put on, to wear [穿了也]

sentences.l: Steel-hard own-coat put-on, I.
sentences.i: I have put on my steel-hard coat.
sentences.n: qataṅγu is the Ming 鋼硬 'steel-hard'; qatan in the next unit is 鋼 'steel'. deġel is a long robe or coat; I take armour from 'steel-hard' and the setting, since the Ming says only 衣裳 'clothes'. emüsbe is emüs- 'put on, wear' in the past.

sentences.t: Qatan žida-ban bariba bi.

morph.gloss: to take hold of, to grasp [拿了也]

sentences.l: Steel own-spear taken, I.
sentences.i: I have taken up my steel spear.
sentences.n: žida-ban is žida 'spear' with the reflexive-possessive -ban; bariba is bari- 'take hold of' in the past (Ming 拿了也).

sentences.t: Qadqurasutu sumun(i)-jan onolaba bi.

words.reading: 中合惕中忽舌剌速禿 Qadqurasutu

morph.gloss: (stem unclear; Ming 有挑皮的 'having a lifted skin'; some kind of arrow-head, uncertain) [有挑皮的]
to nock, to fit to the string (from onor 'nock'; Ming 扣了) [扣了也]

sentences.l: Qadqurasu-having own-arrow nocked, I.
sentences.i: I have set my arrow to the string.
sentences.n: qadqurasutu has the Ming gloss 有挑皮的, which I cannot resolve; it is probably a kind of arrow-head, but I only guess that from the context. onolaba is onola- 'put on the nock' from onor 'nock', Ming 扣了也. qadqurasutu is left untranslated in i.

sentences.t: Qaγ̇ad- Merkid-tür qadquldun morilaja, böġed keġen ügüle.

morph.gloss: the Qa'at, a Merkid clan (Ming 姓氏 'clan name'; the hyphen carries over to the next word) [姓氏]

words.reading: 篾舌兒乞惕-途舌兒 Merkid-tür

morph.gloss: the Merkid, a people [(種名) 行]
to fight, skirmish (stem inferred; Ming 厮殺 'fight') [厮殺︀]
converb that closes a quotation: saying
to speak, to say (bare stem, here an imperative: 'say!') [說]

sentences.l: Qaγ̇ad-Merkid-against fighting, let-us-mount, then saying, say!
sentences.i: Let us ride and fight the Qa'at Merkid. Say so.
sentences.n: Qaγ̇ad- ends in a hyphen in the print because the word is broken at the line; it carries on into Merkid-tür (Ming 種名 行, 'against the Merkid'). qadquldun is qadqu- 'fight' with the reciprocal -ldu- ('one another', as the Ming 厮殺 suggests) and the converb -n; the stem is inferred. morilaja is mori 'horse' made a verb with -la- and the hortative -ja, 'let us mount'. böġed keġen is 'then, saying'; ügüle is the imperative 'say!', which closes the message Jamuqa is giving his carriers. A second round of the same lines follows, now against the Uduid.

sentences.t: Urtu qaraγ̇atu tuk(i)-jan sačuba bi.

morph.gloss: a far view (stem inferred from qara- 'to look'; Ming 遠看見的 'seen from afar') [遠看見的]
standard, banner (so read; the Ming 英頭 is 'hero-head' and the stem is uncertain) [英頭 自的行]
to sprinkle a libation, to sacrifice (stem inferred; Ming 祭了也) [祭了也]

sentences.l: Long far-seen own-banner sprinkled, I.
sentences.i: I have made offering to my long banner, seen from afar.
sentences.n: urtu is 'long' (Ming 長). The Ming repeats 遠看見的 and 英頭 as above; the line begins a second sequence like the first.

sentences.t: Hüker-ün arasu-bar bürigsen ödgen daγ̇utu köġürge-ban deledbe bi.

morph.gloss: skin, hide (Ming 皮子; the final n of arasun is absent, uncertain) [皮子 敎]
instrumental: with, by means of (back-vowel form)
to cover, to stretch over (stem inferred; Ming 幔了的) [幔了的]
dull, thick, of a sound (Ming 濁 'muddy, turbid'; analysis uncertain) [濁]
to beat, to strike (stem inferred; Ming 打了也) [打了也]

sentences.l: Ox's hide-with covered, dull voiced drum my-own beaten, I.
sentences.i: I have beaten my drum, covered in ox hide, with its dull voice.
sentences.n: hüker-ün is 'of the ox' and arasu-bar the instrumental of hide, the n of arasun being lost before the ending. ödgen has the Ming 濁 'muddy, cloudy' and I take it as a deep, dull sound; uncertain.

sentences.t: Oroγ qur- dun(i)-jan unuba bi.

morph.gloss: black-backed, with a black spine (adjective; Ming 黑脊) [黑脊]
fast; a fast horse (the word is split across two printed tokens, qur- / dun(i)-jan) [快馬]
second half of qurdun (the word is split across qur- / dun(i)-jan; see the previous token) [自的行]

sentences.l: Black-backed fast-horse own rode, I.
sentences.i: I have mounted my black-backed fast horse.
sentences.n: oroγ (Ming 黑脊 'black-spined') is a horse colour. The word qurdun is cut across two printed tokens, qur- and dun(i)-jan; the Ming glosses them as 快馬 and 自的行, so I give the second token its own entry as the second half and the reflexive.

sentences.t: hüdesütü qujag(i)-jan emüsbe bi.

morph.gloss: thong, stitching of hide (stem inferred; Ming 皮穿來的 'threaded with hide') [皮穿來的]
armour, mail-coat (noun; Ming 甲) [甲 自的行]
to put on, to wear [穿了也]

sentences.l: Hide-sewn own-armour put-on, I.
sentences.i: I have put on my hide-laced armour.
sentences.n: hüdesütü has the Ming 皮穿來的 'threaded with hide'; hüdesü is my guess at the stem, 'thong, stitching' and -tü is 'having'. qujag(i)-jan is armour (Ming 甲) with the reflexive-possessive. emüsbe as above.

sentences.t: Oṅgitu üldü-beġen bariba bi.

morph.gloss: haft, handle (stem inferred; Ming 抦 'handle') [抦有的]
sword, scimitar (Ming 環刀 'ring-sword') [環刀 自的行]
to take hold of, to grasp [拿了也]

sentences.l: Hilt-having own-sabre taken, I.
sentences.i: I have taken up my hilted sabre.
sentences.n: oṅgitu has the Ming 抦 (a variant of 柄 'handle') and -tu 'having'. üldü is the Ming 環刀 'ring-sword'; -beġen is the reflexive-possessive in a longer form. bariba as above.

sentences.t: Onortu sumun(i)-jan onolaba bi.

morph.gloss: nock, the notch of an arrow [扣子 有的]
to nock, to fit to the string (from onor 'nock'; Ming 扣了) [扣了也]

sentences.l: Nock-having own-arrow nocked, I.
sentences.i: I have fitted my notched arrow to the string.
sentences.n: onortu is onor 'nock' with -tu 'having' (Ming 扣子 有的); onolaba is the verb from it. The same shape as qadqurasutu above.

sentences.t: Uduid-Merkid-tür üküldüje böġed keġen ügüle.

words.reading: 兀都︀亦惕-篾舌兒乞惕-途舌兒 Uduid-Merkid-tür

glyphs.s: 兀都︀亦惕-篾舌兒乞惕-途舌兒

to die (stem uncertain; read from the Ming 捨死 'give up life') [捨死厮殺︀咱]

sentences.l: Uduid-Merkid-against, let-us-fight-to-the-death, then saying, say!
sentences.i: Let us fight the Uduid Merkid to the death. Say so.
sentences.n: üküldüje has the Ming 捨死厮殺咱 'staking death, fight'; I give it ükü- 'die' with the reciprocal -ldü- (as in qadquldun) and the hortative -je, 'let us fight to the death'; uncertain. uduid-merkid-tür is the name of the clan with the people name and the dative-locative.

morph.gloss: To'oril, a man's name (personal name) [(人)名]
ruler, khan (title, set after the name) [皇帝]

words.reading: 不舌峏中罕-中合勒都︀訥 Burqan-Qaldun-u

glyphs.s: 不舌峏中罕-中合勒都︀訥

morph.gloss: Burqan Qaldun, the sacred mountain (Ming 山名) [山名 的]
front, the near side (Ming (前); the same word as 'bosom') [(前)行]
Temüjin, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

glyphs.s: 孛脫中罕-孛斡舌兒只-荅

morph.gloss: Botoqan-Boqorji, a place name (one two-part name) [地名 行]
to appoint, to agree on a meeting (stem inferred; Ming 約會; compare bolžaγ̇an, bolžal) [約會咱]

sentences.l: Toγ̇oril Qān elder-brother when-mounting, Burqan-Qaldun's front-along, Temüžin sworn-brother (acc.) passing-by, coming, Onan river's head-at, Botoqan-Boγ̇orži-at, let-us-fix-a-meeting,
sentences.i: When Qan To'oril, my elder brother, mounts, let him come along the front of Burqan Qaldun, pass by my sworn brother Temüjin, and let us fix a meeting at Botoqan-Boqorji, at the head of the Onan river,
sentences.n: ebür(i)-jer: ebür is 'front' (also 'bosom'), and -jer is an ending with the shape of the instrumental that the Ming glosses only (前)行, the dative-locative sign; 'along' is read from the shape (compare -jer after mör(i)- in the published parts). daγ̇ariγ̇ad (Ming 經過) is 'having passed'. anda-ji is the accusative of anda, so Temüjin is the one passed. bolžalduja is bolža- 'appoint' with the reciprocal -ldu- and the hortative -ja, 'let us fix a meeting between us' (Ming 約會咱). Botoqan-Boγ̇orži is the name of the place (地名).

sentences.t: endēče morilarun Onan müren öġede anda-jin ulus ende bi.

morph.gloss: this; here the locative stem end- [自這裏]
the Onan, the river of Chinggis's homeland (Ming 河名) [河名]
upstream, up (adverb; the Ming here is 送着 'seeing along', unlike 逆着 at word 339; the sense is taken from the later uses, uncertain) [送着]
sworn brother, pledged friend [契合 的]
is, are (verb, short form; Ming 有) [有]

sentences.l: From-here when-mounting, Onan river up, the sworn-brother's people here are.
sentences.i: When I mount from here and go up the Onan, my sworn brother's people are here.
sentences.n: endēče is ene 'this' in the ablative with a long vowel, 'from here', Ming 自這裏. öġede is read 'upstream, up', but the Ming at this token is 送着 'seeing along', not the 逆着 of the later occurrences; the reading rests on those. anda-jin ulus is 'sworn-brother's people'. bi is 'is, are' (Ming 有), not 'I'.

sentences.t: Anda-jin ulus-ača nigen tümen, bi endēče nigen tümen qojar tümen bolžu
